_meta.source: spikes/brain/out/validation.json (uv run python -m flylab.brain --validate), condensed by spikes/dashboard/make_brain_validation.py; numbers copied, not recomputed
_meta.side_note: Notebook code comments: sugar GRNs 'right', id_mn9 'left' (old inverted FAFB convention). Paper text (true biological side): left-hemisphere GRN activation. FlyWire v783 annotation agrees with the paper text: GRNs side=left, MN9_a side=right (contralateral), MN9_b side=left (ipsilateral).
_meta.silencing_semantics: silence = outgoing synapses set to 0 (model.py silence()); silenced neurons are reported with effective rate 0 in 'rates', raw spikes in 'silenced_spiking_rates'

checks.claim: Baseline firing of every neuron is 0 Hz (paper: 'The baseline firing of each neuron in our model is 0 Hz')
Sugar GRN activation at 100 Hz robustly activates MN9 in 100% of simulations (paper, shuffle-control text)
checks.ours: MN9_a active in 10/10 trials, 61.6 Hz; MN9_b active in 10/10 trials, 47.6 Hz

checks.claim: w_syn was chosen so that sugar 100 Hz gives roughly 80% of maximal MN9 firing (paper Methods)
checks.agree: partial: MN9 at 100 Hz is clearly sub-maximal but the ratio differs from ~0.8 (paper tuned w_syn on v630; this is v783)

checks.claim: MN9 rate increases with sugar GRN rate (not quoted from the paper; implied by its w_syn tuning to ~80% of maximal MN9 firing at 100 Hz)
Number of responsive neurons: 45 at 10 Hz, 455 at 200 Hz sugar (paper, v630 with 127,400 neurons, 30 trials)
checks.ours: 40 at 10 Hz, 437 at 200 Hz including the 20 stimulated GRNs (20 / 417 without them); v783, 138639 neurons, 10 trials (fewer trials -> fewer rarely-firing neurons counted)
checks.agree: approximate only (different connectome version and trial count; the paper does not state whether its count includes the stimulated GRNs)

checks.claim: Unilateral sugar GRN activation drives the contralateral MN9 more strongly than the ipsilateral MN9 (paper Fig. 1c)
Sanity (not a paper claim): silencing the stimulated sugar GRNs removes their output, so MN9 must stay at 0 Hz
Bitter GRNs do not activate MN9 and suppress sugar-evoked MN9 firing (paper Fig. 3a)
checks.ours: bitter alone MN9 max = 0.0 Hz; sugar+bitter = 12.3 Hz vs sugar alone 61.6 Hz

checks.claim: Number of responsive neurons with the paper's trial count (30 x 1 s): 45 at 10 Hz, 455 at 200 Hz
checks.ours: 45 at 10 Hz, 447 at 200 Hz including the 20 GRNs (25 / 427 without them)
checks.agree: close if the paper counts the GRNs (45 vs 45, 447 vs 455); v630 vs v783 connectome

brian2_crosscheck.what: same LIF equations simulated with Brian2 (reference implementation of Shiu et al.) on a sugar-GRN subnetwork, 100 Hz stimulation
